question: How do I trace a custom multi-turn agent in Python?
answer:
Use the Weave agent tracing helpers. Wrap the whole session in `weave.start_conversation()`, each user exchange in `weave.start_turn()`, and the model and tool calls inside each turn in `weave.start_llm()` and `weave.start_tool()` [S5]. I haven't run this code. It's adapted from the docs' quickstart.

```python
import weave
weave.init("TEAM/PROJECT")

def run_turn(history, user_message):
    history.append({"role": "user", "content": user_message})
    with weave.start_turn(user_message=user_message, model="gpt-4o-mini"):
        with weave.start_llm(model="gpt-4o-mini", provider_name="openai") as llm:
            answer = call_your_model(history)      # your code
            llm.output(answer)
        # for tool calls:
        # with weave.start_tool(name=..., arguments=..., tool_call_id=...) as tool:
        #     tool.result = run_tool(...)
        return answer

with weave.start_conversation(agent_name="my-agent"):
    history = []
    for q in ["First question", "Follow-up"]:
        run_turn(history, q)
```

- **Setup:** Install `weave`, `openai` and `requests` (the quickstart's packages) [S6]. Call `weave.init("TEAM/PROJECT")`. It authenticates with Weights & Biases and configures the OpenTelemetry (OTel) exporter that sends agent spans to the **Agents** view [S3].
- **Nesting:** In the quickstart, each turn opens a `chat` span for the LLM call. If the model requests a tool, an `execute_tool` span wraps the tool call. A second `chat` span then produces the final answer [S5].
- **Usage and cost:** Inside an LLM span, `llm.record(usage=weave.Usage(...), response_id=..., response_model=...)` sets token usage, the priced model, and the response ID in one call [S5].

The docs say Weave is built on OTel. Each turn, LLM call and tool call emits a span tagged with GenAI attributes such as `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id` [S2]. Traces appear in the project's **Agents** tab, with a multi-turn timeline of nested tool calls, token usage and feedback [S2].

If you use `@weave.op` to trace individual functions, the docs point to a different guide, "Trace LLM applications" [S2]. If your agent already uses an SDK such as the Claude Agent SDK or Codex, the docs suggest an integration instead [S1].

I only read the quickstart's example and the overview page. I didn't read the reference sections on the manual start/end pattern or the semantic conventions.

# Quickstart: Set up custom agent observability

> Trace a multi-turn agent with the Weave SDK. Conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool calls render in the Agents view of your project.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/get-started/custom-agents.md).

[Try in Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/github/wandb/examples/blob/main/colabs/weave/custom-agents-quickstart.ipynb) · [GitHub source](https://github.com/wandb/examples/blob/main/colabs/weave/custom-agents-quickstart.ipynb)

The Weave SDK lets you trace agents built with popular SDKs or custom harnesses. This quickstart shows you how to manually integrate Weave into a custom-built multi-turn agent to emit and capture OpenTelemetry spans. For conceptual understanding about Weave for agents, see [Trace your agents](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents.md).

If you're looking to integrate Weave with SDKs or harnesses such as the Claude Agent SDK or Codex, see [Choose an agent integration](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/agent-integration-quickstart.md). Weave autopatches into several agent-building SDKs and agent harnesses for quick integration.

sources.text:
# Trace your agents

> Use the Weave SDK to instrument multi-turn agentic applications and view them in the Agents tab.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/instrument.md).

Learn how to instrument a multi-turn agentic application using the W\&B Weave SDK so that you can view, debug, and evaluate your agent's behavior. This guide is intended for developers who build or integrate agents and want structured visibility into conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool executions.

The Weave SDK for Agents models the full lifecycle of a multi-turn agent conversation: the agent that owns many conversations, the conversation that groups turns together, each user-agent exchange (turn), the LLM calls within a turn, and the tool executions that an LLM triggers. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project. Each conversation shows a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage, and feedback.

Weave is built on [OpenTelemetry (OTel)](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/), the open standard for distributed tracing. Every turn, LLM call, and tool call emits an OTel *span* (a structured record of one operation). Each span is tagged with [GenAI semantic-convention](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`.

If you're tracing individual functions as Ops with the `@weave.op` decorator, see [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) instead.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/get-started/custom-agents.md).

[Try in Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/github/wandb/examples/blob/main/colabs/weave/custom-agents-quickstart.ipynb) · [GitHub source](https://github.com/wandb/examples/blob/main/colabs/weave/custom-agents-quickstart.ipynb)

The Weave SDK lets you trace agents built with popular SDKs or custom harnesses. This quickstart shows you how to manually integrate Weave into a custom-built multi-turn agent to emit and capture OpenTelemetry spans. For conceptual understanding about Weave for agents, see [Trace your agents](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents.md).

If you're looking to integrate Weave with SDKs or harnesses such as the Claude Agent SDK or Codex, see [Choose an agent integration](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/agent-integration-quickstart.md). Weave autopatches into several agent-building SDKs and agent harnesses for quick integration.

results.title: Integrations overview
results.heading: Trace agents
results.snippet:
## Trace agents

Use these integrations when you're building multi-turn agentic applications and want sessions, turns, and tool calls to appear in the Weave **Agents** view. For agent SDKs, harnesses, and custom instrumentation, see [Choose an agent integration](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/agent-integration-quickstart.md).

Agent SDKs run one turn per call. To group turns into a conversation, pass the SDK's own session or group identifier on every turn. The integration page for each SDK shows which identifier to use.

results.title: Choose an agent integration
results.heading: Custom agents and OpenTelemetry
results.snippet:
## Custom agents and OpenTelemetry

If your agent isn't built with one of the SDKs above, or it already emits OpenTelemetry spans, use the Weave SDK directly. Weave accepts any OTel span and gives special handling to [GenAI semantic-convention attributes](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/gen-ai-agent-spans/) so spans render in the **Agents** view:

* [Quickstart: Manually instrument an agent](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/custom-agents-quickstart.md) — a walkthrough of a small multi-turn agent.
* [Trace your agents](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents.md) — the full reference of agent helpers and concepts.
* [Send OpenTelemetry spans to the Agents view](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents-otel.md) — point an existing OTel pipeline at the Weave agents endpoint, with no Weave SDK required.

results.title: Bedrock Agents
results.heading: Multi-turn conversations
results.snippet:
## Multi-turn conversations

Bedrock Agents preserve conversation state on the service side when you reuse a `sessionId`. To group multiple turns into a single trace in the Weights & Biases UI, wrap the turns in `weave.thread`:

```python lines theme={"system"}
with weave.thread("support-conversation") as t:
    for prompt in [
        "I can't log in to my account.",
        "I already tried resetting my password.",
    ]:
        ask_agent(prompt, session_id=t.thread_id)
```

Weave displays each turn in the UI as individual rows in the Threads view.

results.title: Pi extension
results.heading: Next steps
results.snippet:
### Next steps

To turn this example into a multi-turn conversation, add more prompts. Weave traces each call to `session.prompt()` as a separate `invoke_agent` span, all nested under a single root span. The agent retains context across prompts automatically.

After running the code, the **Agents** tab shows the full multi-turn timeline with nested LLM calls, tool executions, token usage, and cost.

results.heading: Get started
results.snippet:
## Get started

To view signals for your project:

1. Navigate to [Forge](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and select your project.
2. In the sidebar menu, select **Agents** to view all agent conversations saved for your project.
3. In the tab bar, select **Signals**.

![The Signals tab showing a list of scored turns for the agent.](https://mintcdn.com/coreweave-dbfa0e8d/3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx/products/wandb/weave/_media/agent-view-signals.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx\&q=85\&s=8c6cbeb0985f1892769e14cbf70fb16c)

results.title: Trace your agents
results.heading: How data appears in the Weights & Biases UI
results.snippet:
## How data appears in the Weights & Biases UI

After you instrument your agent with the preceding patterns and run it, your traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project at `https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb/[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]/weave/agents`.

* The **Conversations tab** shows all conversations with a minimap of turn activity.
* The **Conversation detail view** opens when you click a conversation and shows all turns, its LLM calls, tool executions, token counts, and any attached feedback.

For details on viewing Agents data in Weave, see [View agent activity](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-activity.md).

results.title: Score agent turns with a remote scorer
results.heading: Score agent turns with a remote scorer
results.snippet:
# Score agent turns with a remote scorer

> Score Weave agent turns with your own HTTP endpoint and see the results as tags or ratings on the Signals tab.

A remote scorer signal scores each completed agent turn with an HTTP endpoint that you host, instead of with an LLM judge. When a turn ends, the Weave agent scoring worker sends the turn to your endpoint in an HTTP `POST` and records the response as feedback on the turn. The result appears as a tag or rating on the **Signals** tab of the [Agents view](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-signals.md).

This page covers remote scorers for agent turns. To score Calls traced with `@weave.op`, see [Score Calls with remote scorers](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/remote-scorers.md). You configure remote scorers with the Python SDK or the Weave UI. The TypeScript SDK doesn't include `RemoteScorer`.

* Infrastructure: Processing is powered by CoreWeave compute and CoreWeave GPUs for scalability across millions of traces.

# Trace your agents

> Use the Weave SDK to instrument multi-turn agentic applications and view them in the Agents tab.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. Learn how to instrument a multi-turn agentic application using the W\&B Weave SDK so that you can view, debug, and evaluate your agent's behavior. This guide is intended for developers who build or integrate agents and want structured visibility into conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool executions.

The Weave SDK for Agents models the full lifecycle of a multi-turn agent conversation: the agent that owns many conversations, the conversation that groups turns together, each user-agent exchange (turn), the LLM calls within a turn, and the tool executions that an LLM triggers. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project. Each conversation shows a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage, and feedback.

Weave is built on [OpenTelemetry (OTel)](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/), the open standard for distributed tracing. Every turn, LLM call, and tool call emits an OTel *span* (a structured record of one operation). Each span is tagged with [GenAI semantic-convention](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`.

If you're tracing individual functions as Ops with the `@weave.op` decorator, see [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) instead.

Use the Weave agent tracing helpers. Wrap the whole session in `weave.start_conversation()`, each user exchange in `weave.start_turn()`, and the model and tool calls inside each turn in `weave.start_llm()` and `weave.start_tool()` [S5]. I haven't run this code. It's adapted from the docs' quickstart.

```python
import weave
weave.init("TEAM/PROJECT")

def run_turn(history, user_message):
    history.append({"role": "user", "content": user_message})
    with weave.start_turn(user_message=user_message, model="gpt-4o-mini"):
        with weave.start_llm(model="gpt-4o-mini", provider_name="openai") as llm:
            answer = call_your_model(history)      # your code
            llm.output(answer)
        # for tool calls:
        # with weave.start_tool(name=..., arguments=..., tool_call_id=...) as tool:
        #     tool.result = run_tool(...)
        return answer

with weave.start_conversation(agent_name="my-agent"):
    history = []
    for q in ["First question", "Follow-up"]:
        run_turn(history, q)
```

- **Setup:** Install `weave`, `openai` and `requests` (the quickstart's packages) [S6]. Call `weave.init("TEAM/PROJECT")`. It authenticates with Weights & Biases and configures the OpenTelemetry (OTel) exporter that sends agent spans to the **Agents** view [S3].
- **Nesting:** In the quickstart, each turn opens a `chat` span for the LLM call. If the model requests a tool, an `execute_tool` span wraps the tool call. A second `chat` span then produces the final answer [S5].
- **Usage and cost:** Inside an LLM span, `llm.record(usage=weave.Usage(...), response_id=..., response_model=...)` sets token usage, the priced model, and the response ID in one call [S5].

The docs say Weave is built on OTel. Each turn, LLM call and tool call emits a span tagged with GenAI attributes such as `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id` [S2]. Traces appear in the project's **Agents** tab, with a multi-turn timeline of nested tool calls, token usage and feedback [S2].

If you use `@weave.op` to trace individual functions, the docs point to a different guide, "Trace LLM applications" [S2]. If your agent already uses an SDK such as the Claude Agent SDK or Codex, the docs suggest an integration instead [S1].

I only read the quickstart's example and the overview page. I didn't read the reference sections on the manual start/end pattern or the semantic conventions.
